title: A CALL TO DEAL WITH SIN

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: So Moses said to Israel's judges, "Each of you must put to death those of your men who have yoked themselves to the Baal of Peor." Then an Israelite man brought into the camp a Midianite woman right before the eyes of Moses and the whole assembly of Israel while they were weeping at the entrance to the tent of meeting. - Num 25:5-6 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses passes on God's command to the judges: those who had joined themselves to Baal must be dealt with. This was a moment of national reckoning, a call to root out the sin that had provoked God's anger. The people were weeping at the tent of meeting, some perhaps in genuine repentance over what had happened.

But then comes a stunning act of defiance. In the very midst of this weeping and judgment, an Israelite man brazenly brings a Midianite woman into the camp, right before the eyes of Moses and the whole assembly. While others mourned their sin, this man flaunted his. It was open, shameless rebellion.

This scene captures two very different responses to sin. Some wept, grieving over how they had grieved God. But this man hardened his heart and paraded his transgression without shame. The same conviction that softened some hardened others. Sin, when unrepented, breeds a boldness that no longer fears God.

We each face this choice when confronted with our sin. Will we weep in repentance, or will we harden ourselves in defiance? The tender heart that mourns its sin is precious to God, while a hardened heart drifts further from Him. In Christ we are given hearts that can grieve over sin and turn back to God (2 Cor 7:10). May yours be a heart that weeps rather than one that hardens.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When confronted with your sin, do you soften or harden?
2. What does genuine grief over sin look like in your life?
3. How can you keep your heart tender toward God's conviction?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, keep my heart tender before You. When I am confronted with my sin, let me weep in repentance rather than harden myself in defiance, and turn me back to You. Amen.
